rules.title: Prohibition on sale of coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Selling, licensing or otherwise providing to City of Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley is unlawful. A coordinated pricing algorithm is a process that uses nonpublic Competitor Data less than 90 days old to calculate and recommend rent prices, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms in coordination between a Berkeley landlord and its competitors, including through a third-party vendor.
rules.coverage_text: Anyone who sells, licenses or provides coordinated pricing algorithms to City of Berkeley landlords for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: Excluded from the definition: products that publish aggregated and anonymous rental data without recommending rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms; products used to set rent or income limits under government affordable housing guidelines; products or processes used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development, as long as Competitor Data is not used as an input when a recommendation is calculated for a Berkeley landlord.
rules.penalty: The City Attorney may file a civil action for damages, injunctive relief, restitution/return of illegal profits, and/or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation; the court shall award reasonable attorney's fees and costs to the City Attorney if it prevails.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Prohibition on landlord use of coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use a coordinated pricing algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley. Each month a violation continues and each unit for which the algorithm was used is a separate violation.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords of residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: Excluded from the definition: products that publish aggregated and anonymous rental data without recommending rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms; products used to set rent or income limits under government affordable housing guidelines; products or processes used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development, as long as Competitor Data is not used as an input when a recommendation is calculated for a Berkeley landlord.
rules.penalty: The City Attorney may sue for damages, injunctive relief, restitution/return of illegal profits, and/or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. An aggrieved tenant may sue for injunctive relief, money damages, and/or civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, with reasonable attorney's fees and costs awarded to a prevailing tenant; lease provisions limiting such fees are unenforceable.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. Each separate month that a violation exists or continues, and each separate residential dwelling unit for which the landlord used the coordinated pricing algorithm, shall constitute a separate and distinct violation.
